core.title: OptiMat Alloys: a FAIR-aligned living database of multi-principal element alloys enabled by a conversational agent
core.abstract: Abstract Existing FAIR materials repositories can only serve pre-computed entries, so broad coverage is perpetually incomplete and cannot adapt to new questions on demand. We present OptiMat Alloys, a large language model-powered conversational agent for multi-principal element alloy exploration. Its central contribution is LLM-based workflow orchestration coupled to a living database : every calculation is performed on demand and persisted automatically with provenance in a local database, so asking a question produces provenance-rich, FAIR-aligned records without a separate deposition step. The agent is accessible through a web interface that requires no programming expertise ( low-barrier accessibility ) and reports uncertainty through cross-potential and cross-configuration validation ( built-in uncertainty quantification ). By coupling foundational machine learning interatomic potentials that cover nearly the entire periodic table with natural-language interaction, OptiMat Alloys enables targeted, on-demand computation guided by the user’s domain knowledge and brings computational alloy screening within reach of any materials scientist.
core.summary: 本文针对合金组合空间庞大、模拟门槛高及计算结果难以持续复用的问题，将对话式工作流编排、通用机器学习原子间势与本地数据库连接起来，实现按需计算和来源信息自动保存。[P1–P4]验证涵盖材料性质、智能体执行及缓存复用，但结果仍属初筛级；跨模型一致不代表物理准确，跨用户汇聚也尚未实现。[P6–P9]阅读重点是计算与知识积累的一体化机制，而非将其视为自主发现或平衡相预测系统。

deep_read.problem: 既有材料数据库主要服务预计算条目，难以响应新成分和新性质问题；新增结果还需研究者主动整理提交。作者希望同时降低模拟操作门槛、扩大数据供给，并补充可信度信息。问题核心不是单纯增加条目，而是让日常提问持续产生可追踪、可复用的研究记录。[P1–P3]
deep_read.method: 系统以AutoGen和ASE连接七项工具，完成SQS生成、两阶段FIRE弛豫、弹性张量及QHA计算，再将性质与来源信息保存至SQLite。科学约束置于工具层，LLM负责请求解析和工具串联；跨势函数、构型与尺寸比较用于观察预测离散和收敛。[P4][P17–P19]
deep_read.innovation: 作者强调的贡献是将LLM编排与自动持久化结合，让计算和入库成为同一步骤，并以低编程门槛界面支持持续使用。解读：创新主要在科研基础设施的组织机制，而非新势函数或新物理理论；当前已实现的是实例内累积复用，不是社区级联邦数据库。[P3][P9][P14]
deep_read.findings: 作者单实例积累491个结构；28种合金验证中，晶格参数MAE≤0.011 Å、形成能MAE≤0.014 eV/atom。缓存比较无需新计算，但智能体曾在正确数值上给出错误排序及延性解释，说明工具执行可靠与文字结论可靠必须分开评估。[P6][P9][P13]

随机单相模型不含有序与分相，集合离散不能覆盖共同偏差，联邦尚未实现。[P16–P17]原文件问题包括[P2]正文与图1b数量级冲突，限制空间规模引用；[P8]表2上下界矛盾，限制加速比解释；[P23]文献120缺编号，影响溯源。没有缺失公式可供补推。

deep_read.connection: 解读：与结构设计的直接联系是成分—弹性及热学性质初筛；与可靠性研究的联系是区分构型波动、模型偏差和解释错误。对智能运维，来源追踪、缓存复用和稳定性标记具有迁移潜力，但论文没有设备监测、故障诊断或寿命预测验证。[P6][P18–P19]
deep_read.next_steps: 建议先选定目标合金族，使用已存构型复现并锁定软件与势函数版本，再开展多构型、多计算器及针对性DFT验证。延性比较应统一平均方案，解释规则宜在工具层校验。作者规划的DFT触发与微调闭环尚未实现，不应作为现有功能使用。[P17–P20]

core.title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
core.abstract: Abstract Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

core.title: Machine psychology for language models
core.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a “machine psychology” for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.

core.title: A physics-informed LLM agent for uncovering typhoon- and earthquake-induced turbine failures and offline yaw-pitch countermeasures.
core.abstract: Extreme typhoons and earthquakes can cause severe damage to wind turbine structures, underscoring the need to better understand failure mechanisms and potential mitigation strategies. This study develops Iwind, a physics-informed large language model agent for wind-turbine engineering analysis. Supported by domain-specific training and multi-path retrieval-augmented generation, Iwind combines ReAct-style reasoning with the model context protocol to invoke the in-house physics solver Zwind for natural-language-driven load simulations. In the reported evaluations, Iwind outperformed its parent model on wind-turbine knowledge tasks and supported load-simulation execution and visual damage inspection. The collected cases showed blade fractures, tower buckling, and overturning under typhoon loading, while some earthquake-damaged turbines showed more pronounced damage in foundations or lower supporting structures. Parametric Zwind simulations further revealed W- and M-shaped offline yaw-pitch response manifolds for the investigated typhoon and earthquake cases, respectively, providing simulation-derived references for parked-state comparison and hazard-region identification.

deep_read.findings: 作者单实例积累491个结构；28种合金验证中，晶格参数MAE≤0.011 Å、形成能MAE≤0.014 eV/atom。缓存比较无需新计算，但智能体曾在正确数值上给出错误排序及延性解释，说明工具执行可靠与文字结论可靠必须分开评估。[P6][P9][P13]
deep_read.limitations:
随机单相模型不含有序与分相，集合离散不能覆盖共同偏差，联邦尚未实现。[P16–P17]原文件问题包括[P2]正文与图1b数量级冲突，限制空间规模引用；[P8]表2上下界矛盾，限制加速比解释；[P23]文献120缺编号，影响溯源。没有缺失公式可供补推。

deep_read.connection: 解读：与结构设计的直接联系是成分—弹性及热学性质初筛；与可靠性研究的联系是区分构型波动、模型偏差和解释错误。对智能运维，来源追踪、缓存复用和稳定性标记具有迁移潜力，但论文没有设备监测、故障诊断或寿命预测验证。[P6][P18–P19]
deep_read.next_steps: 建议先选定目标合金族，使用已存构型复现并锁定软件与势函数版本，再开展多构型、多计算器及针对性DFT验证。延性比较应统一平均方案，解释规则宜在工具层校验。作者规划的DFT触发与微调闭环尚未实现，不应作为现有功能使用。[P17–P20]

papers.title: Visual LLM-guided consensus spatial domain detection with L-STAR
papers.abstract: Abstract Spatial transcriptomics measures gene activity while preserving the locations of cells within tissue. A key analysis step is to divide the tissue into spatial domains, but the performance of computational methods varies considerably across datasets, and no single method consistently performs best. Here we show that a large language model can compare spatial domain maps and identify the better-performing methods. We developed L-STAR, which visually compares and ranks candidate methods, then builds a consensus map from the highest-ranked results. Across datasets representing different tissues, species, and technologies, L-STAR matched expert annotations more closely than individual methods or consensus analysis using a fixed set of methods. Its rankings were reproducible and generally stable when image colors or presentation order changed. L-STAR also provided rationales for its comparisons and assigned biologically meaningful names to the detected domains. These findings show that large language models can make spatial transcriptomics analysis more adaptive, robust, and interpretable.

papers.title: Machine psychology for language models
papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) show increasingly advanced emergent capabilities and are being incorporated across various societal domains. Understanding their behavior and reasoning abilities is therefore important. We argue that a fruitful direction for research is engaging LLMs in experiments inspired by psychology that have traditionally been aimed at understanding human cognition and behavior. Here, we highlight and summarize theoretical perspectives, experimental paradigms, and computational analysis techniques that this approach brings to the table. It paves the way for a “machine psychology” for LLMs that goes beyond performance measurements and focuses instead on computational insights that move us toward a better understanding and discovery of emergent abilities and behavioral patterns in LLMs. We review existing work taking this approach, synthesize best practices, and highlight promising future directions. We also describe the important caveats of applying methodologies designed for understanding humans to machines. We posit that leveraging tools from experimental psychology to study LLMs will become increasingly valuable as models evolve to be more powerful, opaque, multimodal, and integrated into complex agentic real-world settings.

papers.title: A physics-informed LLM agent for uncovering typhoon- and earthquake-induced turbine failures and offline yaw-pitch countermeasures.
papers.abstract: Extreme typhoons and earthquakes can cause severe damage to wind turbine structures, underscoring the need to better understand failure mechanisms and potential mitigation strategies. This study develops Iwind, a physics-informed large language model agent for wind-turbine engineering analysis. Supported by domain-specific training and multi-path retrieval-augmented generation, Iwind combines ReAct-style reasoning with the model context protocol to invoke the in-house physics solver Zwind for natural-language-driven load simulations. In the reported evaluations, Iwind outperformed its parent model on wind-turbine knowledge tasks and supported load-simulation execution and visual damage inspection. The collected cases showed blade fractures, tower buckling, and overturning under typhoon loading, while some earthquake-damaged turbines showed more pronounced damage in foundations or lower supporting structures. Parametric Zwind simulations further revealed W- and M-shaped offline yaw-pitch response manifolds for the investigated typhoon and earthquake cases, respectively, providing simulation-derived references for parked-state comparison and hazard-region identification.
